walkthroughs.body_html:
Every atom has a tiny nucleus at its centre and electrons in shells around it.

The nucleus holds protons (+1) and neutrons (0). Electrons are -1 and orbit in shells: 2, 8, 8.

An atom overall is neutral because protons equal electrons.

The atomic number tells you the number of protons.

The mass number is protons + neutrons. So neutrons = mass number - atomic number.

For example, carbon-12 has 6 protons and 6 neutrons.

Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.

The periodic table arranges elements by atomic number. Groups are columns; periods are rows.

Mendeleev left gaps for elements not yet discovered.

mcqs.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.
Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.

mcqs.q: What is different between two isotopes of the same element?
options: Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
Isotopes have different numbers of electrons, which is why their mass differs.
They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

mcqs.q: Why does first ionisation energy generally increase across a period?
options: Atoms get bigger across a period, making electrons easier to add but harder to remove.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays roughly constant, so electrons are held more tightly.

sequence.def: 1803: atoms pictured as tiny indivisible solid spheres
1897: electron discovered; positive ball with electrons inside
1911: gold foil experiment revealed a tiny dense positive nucleus
1913: electrons orbit the nucleus at fixed distances in shells
1932: neutral particle in the nucleus explains isotopes
